Run phased and unphased ancestry splitting on the same BCF + MSP

Source: R/phased.R
ancestry_split_combined.Rd

Parses the VCF/BCF and RFMix MSP file once, then runs both deterministic per-haplotype splitting (split_haplotype_multi) and proportional diploid splitting (split_diploid_multi). Works for any number of populations K \(\ge\) 2.

ancestry_split_combined(vcf_path, msp_path, chrom = NULL, verbose = TRUE)

Arguments

vcf_path

Path to a phased VCF or BCF file. bcftools must be in PATH.

msp_path

Path to an RFMix MSP file (plain text or gzipped TSV).

chrom

Chromosome to process (e.g. "chr19" or "19"). If NULL, all chromosomes present in the VCF are used.

verbose

Print step-by-step progress messages.

Value

Invisibly, a list with two named elements, phased and unphased. Each element is itself a list whose first K entries are named dosage matrices (variants \(\times\) samples), one per population in the order given by the MSP file (e.g. $AFR, $EUR). Additional entries: variant_info, sample_ids, and overlap.

Details

Both splits share the same parsed MSP tracts and VCF genotypes. Diploid ancestry codes are generated automatically from the MSP population codes: pure-ancestry codes are 1 ... K (one per population) and mixed-ancestry codes are K+1 ... K+M where M = K(K-1)/2 enumerates all unordered pairs. Monomorphic variants are filtered independently in each mode.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
res <- ancestry_split_combined(
  vcf_path = "data/chr19.phased.bcf",
  msp_path = "data/chr19.msp.tsv.gz",
  chrom    = "chr19"
)
res$phased$AFR    # deterministic AFR dosage matrix
res$unphased$AFR  # proportional AFR dosage matrix
} # }
